newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand yield curve again closes steeper.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand yield curve again closes steeper.

text.p: New Zealand's yield curve steepened again on Wednesday as bank bills were sold and long bond prices firmed.

Some dealers said the move in the long bonds was disappointing after the FOMC decision to leave rates unchanged but they noted the local market had rallied well on Tuesday and bond yields were approaching the perceived bottom of the range ahead of the October 12 election.
The market is strongly transaction driven at present so some maturities are falling out of line with the curve, depending on flows.
Most economists had picked the FOMC result incorrectly but many dealers say the Fed is simply storing up for a bigger hike next time, probably after the U.S. election.

Dealers were somewhat perplexed why the 90-day bank bills weakened. Some said it may a hangover from Tuesday's stronger than expected wages data, which suggested any easing will be delayed until late in the year or early next year.
Others said there is a feeling the currency may have begun to trend down and the bills are reflecting that.
As well, talk of further euro or dual currency issues appears to have dissipated for the moment.
There was little reaction to August merchandise trade data which showed the deficit rising to $384.8 million from $252.8 million a year ago.
Bancorp said that aside from seasonal factors, the figures showed the results of the exchange rate making exports less competitive and imports more competitive.
